name: maybe_Fs_SetTransferPriority
summary: Applies a per-mode enable/disable mask to the twelve transfer channels stored at self+0x20..+0x50 (5-byte stride table at 0x0072D710) and arms or cancels the bulk transfer when the mode is 4.
evidence: Named caller Fs_CacheSet_Initialize puts this in the nn::fs cache-set init path, and the body is only per-channel enable/disable plus the bulk-transfer arm; 'priority' is still an inference, so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Os_InitTimeoutBase
summary: One-time init of the global timing record at 0x007AEA48: stores ten times the tick period at +0x18, sets the time-source byte at +1 and marks the record usable at +0.
evidence: Only caller Gfx_InitDefaultTexture does not need timeout math, so that caller name is itself doubtful; func_0010BE98/func_0010BE20 (the tick-period getters) still have no readable body and the 'timeout' reading stays unverified.

name: maybe_Os_GetLockDepth
summary: Returns the first word of the global lock object after asserting its busy bit (bit 0 of +4); the assert helper currently carries the misnomer std_RunTerminateHandler, so this is a plain getter whose result caller 0x00104FDC reads as a runtime flag.
evidence: Both callees are misnamed or unnamed, so neither the 'depth' reading nor the lock owner is confirmed; the getter shape (assert then load) is clear.

name: maybe_Os_ShutdownSyncObject
summary: Shuts down the global service object at 0x007AEA10: closes up to eight registered event handles with svcCloseHandle (svc 0x23), unlinks the service list node and clears the state word under the service mutex.
evidence: Only caller is the equally dubious Input_Initialize; the object is the global g_dspServiceState, so 'sync object' should read 'service', but the service identity is not proven by a named caller.

name: maybe_Gfx_SubmitValueCommand
summary: Stores value at record+0x10 and submits one GPU command with header 0x0B0501C8 through Gfx_IpcCmd861.
evidence: No callers at all and the command header 0x0B0501C8 is not decoded anywhere in the named code, so the meaning of the submitted value is still unknown.

name: maybe_Snd_StopVoiceGroup
summary: Stops one sound group: releases its stream context through func_00112E18(&g_csndHardwareState), invalidates four channel ids at +0x4C..+0x4F and clears the active byte.
evidence: The four -1 channel ids and the hardware-state release fit one stream's voices, but there is still no caller that names the object, so 'voice group' remains a struct label.

name: maybe_Snd_GetCommandBlock
summary: Return-only thunk: forwards to 0x001129F4 and returns its result (Ghidra had dropped the return type, hence the explicit void*).
evidence: Still no caller, and 0x001129F4 has no readable body, so even the 'command block' half of the name rests on the neighbouring Snd_ResetChannelUnitsInPlace family.

name: maybe_Save_CompleteAsyncRead
summary: Hands the five request fields at +0x14..+0x24 to Save_AsyncReadWorker and then stores completion state 5 in the shared work object.
evidence: Named callee Save_AsyncReadWorker supports the hand-off, but no readable caller confirms that this is the completion path, and the shared work object's field names (g_gpuChannelSessionHandle) are stale guesses.

name: maybe_Os_HandleInit
summary: Creates a kernel handle into an empty out slot through 0x0012038C and aborts (0xE0A0183B) when the create fails; callers are the OS memory, physical-address and perf-sample helpers.
evidence: Four named callers in different modules (Os_IsInHeapRange, Os_VirtualToPhysical, maybe_Os_PerfSample_Loop, maybe_Fs_ReadRecordWithRetry) confirm a shared helper, but 0x0012038C is unnamed so what kind of handle is created is unknown.

name: maybe_Hid_GetEventObject
signature: u32 maybe_Hid_GetEventObject(HidObject* hidObject, u32* outValue, u32 defaultValue, u32 cmdArg)
summary: Writes the default into *outValue and, when the object has a session handle at +8, sends HID IPC command 0x0C which overwrites it; the function always returns the constant 0xC8A0A7F8.
evidence: Being the only caller of Svc_IpcCmdC0040 fixes the command number but not its meaning, and the constant result carries no information; the Hid_ prefix is still an inference.

name: maybe_Os_StoreThreadLocalValue
summary: Passes the per-thread block (func_0011F730), the current process handle and two caller values to IPC command 8; reached from the memory-free path, so it is an IPC wrapper for the heap, not necessarily a thread-local store.
evidence: Caller is the misnamed maybe_Mem_FreeThroughCallback and the IPC helpers are unnamed, so the thread-local reading stays unverified.

name: maybe_Os_DestroyThreadLocal
summary: At thread exit fetches the thread-local object (func_0011F20C), destroys it via func_0011F730 and issues Gfx_IpcCmd1A0000; does nothing when no object exists.
evidence: Only caller is the misnamed Gfx_IpcCmd50100 and the two callees are unnamed, so the TLS shape is the only support.

name: maybe_Os_WaitSharedBlock
summary: Waits with svcWaitSynchronization1 (svc 0x24) on the handle stored in *state when it is non-zero, aborts on failure, then re-opens the SDK IPC session.
evidence: No callers, and both callees (Os_EnsureIpcSessionOpen, the abort helper) only confirm a wait/session shape, not what object is waited on.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SetTextureFill(u32 src, u32 size, int enable, u32 color)
summary: Queues PICA200 surface work on the GPU message queue at 0x007B0070: optionally a type-5 record carrying src/size, then a type-1 record carrying the fill colour.
evidence: The push target is the named Os_MessageQueue_Push and the record template comes from the texture-blit global, but nothing names the colour/record semantics, so 'fill' is inferred.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelMode(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, int mode, unsigned char priority)
summary: Under the mixer lock, stores the play-mode byte at channel+0xE (and the +0x39 priority byte when the mode is 0) and marks the channel dirty with bit 0x20000; returns 1 when the lock was taken.
evidence: Named caller Snd_UpdateChannelState places it in the mixer update, but the field semantics are still read off offsets and dirty bits only.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord34(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned int value)
summary: Stores a caller-supplied 32-bit word at channel+0x34 and marks the channel dirty with bit 0x40000; same lock/return shape as the other Snd_SetChannel* setters.
evidence: Only caller Snd_UpdateChannelState passes a computed word whose meaning is not visible, so the field stays named by its offset.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelWord3A(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short value)
summary: Stores a 16-bit value at channel+0x3A and marks the channel dirty with bit 0x400000.
evidence: Only the offset, width and dirty bit are hard facts; Snd_UpdateChannelState supplies the value with no field meaning attached.

name: maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams
signature: unsigned int maybe_Snd_SetChannelAdpcmParams(SndMixer* mixer, int channel, unsigned short arg3, unsigned short b, unsigned short c, unsigned short d, unsigned short e)
summary: Writes five consecutive decoder fields of the channel block (+0x40, +0x42, +0x44, +0x46 and the byte at +0x45) and marks the channel dirty with bit 0x1000000.
evidence: Five 16-bit fields written as one block match a decoder parameter set, but the ADPCM reading still rests on the neighbouring +0x24/+0x26 state fields, not on a named caller.

name: maybe_Gfx_CreateChannelBuffers
signature: int maybe_Gfx_CreateChannelBuffers(unsigned int width, unsigned int height, char* mode)
summary: Rounds both dimensions up (+4 below 0x40, +5 above, minimum 8) and creates a pair of 8-bit buffers through Svc_Ir_SetupChannel; on failure it closes the service again.
evidence: No branch reaches this address (dead code) and Svc_Ir_SetupChannel is itself a guessed name, so the subsystem (Snd vs Gfx vs camera) is unproven.

name: Video_IdctSubblocks
summary: Runs the 4x4 inverse transform Video_IdctBlock4x4 once for every set bit of the sub-block mask byte at 0x08010400[subblockIndex], i.e. reconstructs up to four sub-blocks of one macroblock.
evidence: Named callee Video_IdctBlock4x4 (confirmed 4x4 IDCT) is called exactly once per mask bit; the surrounding decompilation is damaged (unaff_r6), but this loop is the whole recovered body, so the name is descriptive rather than guessed.

name: Video_IdctSubblocks_B
summary: Second copy of the per-mask 4x4 inverse-transform loop, calling Video_IdctBlock4x4_B once for each set bit of the sub-block mask byte.
evidence: Body identical to 0x001356D4 apart from the IDCT callee and the constant table address; named callee Video_IdctBlock4x4_B carries the semantics, and the damaged-decompilation flag does not change that.

name: Video_IdctSubblocks_C
summary: Third copy of the per-mask 4x4 inverse-transform loop (track C), calling Video_IdctBlock4x4_C once for each set bit of the sub-block mask byte.
evidence: Same 84-byte template as the confirmed twins 0x001356D4/0x0013BCD4 with the named callee Video_IdctBlock4x4_C; the unaff_r6 damage does not affect the mask-to-IDCT mapping.

name: maybe_SQCommand_Tail
summary: Not a real entry point: a mid-function split inside SQCommand (0x0015179C) whose recovered body is just the tail calls to func_001902B4 and Text_Page_BuildAtOffset.
evidence: Seed symbol SQCommand covers the 2744-byte range containing this address and no branch targets it; the listed callees belong to the enclosing routine.

name: maybe_Gfx_MovieFrame_BuildEntry
signature: u32 maybe_Gfx_MovieFrame_BuildEntry(void* queue, u32 surface, u32 arg3)
summary: Fills two six-word arrays in the movie queue's f_0 sub-structure and advances a wrapping slot index; called for each decoded movie surface by Gfx_MovieQueue_Push.
evidence: The readable body is still halt_baddata (damaged decompilation), so only the named caller Gfx_MovieQueue_Push and the documented ARM push/loop shape support the entry-building reading.

name: maybe_MessageRegistActor_Continuation
summary: Continuation block of MessageRegistActor (0x00159B7C): resolves the slot sprite from ctx->f_8->f_48 through Ui_Overlay_ResolveSlotSprite; not a stand-alone entry point.
evidence: No prologue and no caller; the only user is the parent function, so the label stays a positional one.

name: maybe_Script_ReturnZeroStub2
summary: 16-byte Squirrel native stub that performs the VM stack-slot bookkeeping via Script_SetSlotFromStackAlt and returns 0 (a null result for the script).
evidence: No callers, no strings and a single named callee, so the stub role is clear but which native it implements is not.

name: maybe_Actor_ShowGripNode
summary: Walks the node's child chain (vtable[0] then +0xC) to the entry whose class id equals the inline constant, shows its grip node with Model_Equip_SetGripNode(node, 1, 1, ...) and sets node->f_60 = 1.
evidence: The recovered body (previously unreadable, which is why the old name guessed 'equip part B') calls the named 3D attachment helper Model_Equip_SetGripNode with show=1 and then latches +0x60; its hide twin is 0x00161918.

name: maybe_Actor_HideGripNode
summary: Same walk as 0x00160F14 but calls Model_Equip_SetGripNode(node, 0, 1, ...) and clears node->f_60 = 0, i.e. hides the attached grip/equipment node.
evidence: Recovered body (the old name had no body at all) differs from 0x00160F14 only in the show flag 1 -> 0 and the latched byte; the named callee Model_Equip_SetGripNode carries the semantics.

name: Battle_CommandSlots_TryDecrement
summary: Tentatively decrements the count byte of each of the four 3-byte command slots (+0xFD/+0x100/+0x103/+0x106) whose state byte is 5, validates with Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition(self, 5) and restores all four counts when the condition fails.
evidence: Named callee Battle_CheckUnitCommandCondition(self,5) is exactly the validation of the four slots that were just decremented, and the rollback restores the saved counts; the readable field names (maybe_soundTimerFF ...) are stale and do not describe command slots, which is why the offsets are quoted in the summary.

name: maybe_Container_AddInstanceWithHandle
summary: Inserts an instance into a container table when f_e0 is 1 or kind >= 5: reserves a free slot, stores a generation-wrapped handle from f_e4 (wrapping against the limit at 0x007A8B40+4) and registers through 0x0017C9F8.
evidence: Only caller is the garbage name tP_, and 0x0017C9F8 has no readable body, so 'instance with handle' is still read off the generation counter.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_Refresh
summary: Per-frame refresh of a field scene object: forwards the node update, re-applies the actor movement state (2 when the transform-dirty flag is set, else 0) and resets the animation when the movement succeeded and an anim owner is present.
evidence: Named callees Field_SceneObject_ResetAnimation and Container_IntrusiveList_NotifyAll fit a refresh, but there is no caller and the gating flag at +0x29F is still anonymous.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA
signature: void maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanA(void* self, const TextEntry* entry, u32 word0, u32 word1)
summary: Text-layout span builder: ARM push {r4-r8,lr} prologue plus a style<7 / non-empty-span guard, but the recovered C stops after a mis-marked wcslen call, so only the shape is known.
evidence: Still damaged: the decompiler drops everything after func_00100B74 (which does return), and the only caller is the equally uncertain maybe_Text_DecodeName.

name: maybe_Text_BuildLayoutSpanB
summary: Twin of 0x0018CEA4 (same wcslen-truncated layout-span builder); the recovered body is a single call to func_00100B74.
evidence: The recovered entry point has no dossier and its body is truncated at the same mis-marked call, so neither the span role nor the 'B' distinction is verifiable.

name: maybe_Ui_SetOwnerAndDispatch
summary: Attaches a UI widget to its owner: runs the shared layout prologue drN, stores owner->f_AC at self+0x70, self-links at +0x6C and tail-calls self->f_4C->f_18.
evidence: The only callee is the shared UI prologue drN and the vtable tail is unrecovered, so the attach reading is plausible but not confirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_UnknownPaneSetupC
summary: Unrecoverable: the shared UI prologue drN runs and then the body hits bad instruction data, so no behaviour beyond 'a UI object setup' can be claimed.
evidence: Body is still halt_baddata after drN with no named callers; kept as an explicitly unknown pane setup so the address is not lost.

name: maybe_Ui_InitTransform
summary: Initialises a stack transform/rectangle via 0x006722C4 (a neighbour of the named Gfx_CmdBuf_WriteMeshPartCommands) before the body truncates.
evidence: Both callers (maybe_Battle_Calc_DamageTable, maybe_Ui_ProfileScreen_ConfirmSelection) are themselves uncertain and the rest of the body is lost, so the transform reading is still positional.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_HandlePaneStackInput
summary: Window pane-stack input step: input bit 4 pops the pane stack, bit 1 feeds the cursor/gauge value into Ui_Gauge_AddValue, and bits 0x102 push the detail pane via Ui_Window_PushPane.
evidence: The recovered body (there was none before) calls the named Ui_Window_PushPane / Ui_Window_PopPane on self->paneStack, which pins the operation to the pane stack; the window class itself is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelNode_Dtor
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelNode_Dtor(void* self, u32 vtable, u32 owner)
summary: Destructor of a UI object derived from the composite window: reinstalls the class vtable and then the shared g_uiCompositeWindowVtable, unlinks three intrusive list node pairs, releases the owner sub-objects through Ui_DialogRoot_DtorAlt and frees the block.
evidence: The g_uiCompositeWindowVtable store proves a composite-window base, but no vtable row or caller identifies the concrete class, so 'PanelNode' stays a placeholder.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ShowSimple
summary: Starts a simple message in a message window: copies the record word into wnd->f_b0->f_136 and sets state 7, style 2 and field 6 before the body truncates.
evidence: Callers include the equally uncertain Field_ShowSimpleMessage and Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState, so the show path is supported but no named caller proves the 'simple' variant.

name: maybe_Ui_SceneFlow_OnOpen
summary: Scene-flow open step: applies a transform, rebinds the 2D layer when the state style byte is not -1, then fires cut-scene command 4 through Event_OnCutSceneCommand.
evidence: The readable body is still mostly lost (func_0011FFD8 / func_002F25A0 dummies) and the only caller is the uncertain maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_OnDecide.

name: maybe_Gfx_Sprite2D_Refresh
summary: Truncated Thumb routine whose only recovered action is Ui_Balloon_UpdateAnchorPosition plus 'return 0'; the six named callees suggest a 2D sprite/actor refresh.
evidence: No callers, and only one of the six callees survives in the decompiled body, so neither the class nor what is refreshed is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_ResourceSetOwner_Dtor
summary: Destructor thunk for a UI object embedding a Ui_ResourceSet at +0x38: installs the class vtable, runs Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor on the embedded bundle and returns the adjusted base pointer (this-0x38).
evidence: The vptr store plus adjusted return is the standard destructor-thunk shape and the callee Ui_ResourceSet_Dtor is confident, but no caller or vtable row names the owning class.

name: maybe_Ui_ItemScreen_Cancel
summary: Step handler that waits for the text scroll (Ui_TextScroll_IsFinished); when it is finished it tears down the list widgets, notifies the screen vtable +0x5C and switches to the next handler pair from g_uiItemScreenSelectCallbacks.
evidence: Named callees Ui_TextScroll_IsFinished and Shop_SellItem confirm the shop/item screen, but no caller names the cancel/back verb.

name: maybe_Ui_State_SetState2
summary: Initialises a transition record with the 0xFF/0xFFFF invalid defaults, notifies the active screen through the manager vtable +0x5C, sets screen command 2 via func_001C0F28 and copies the handler pair from g_uiItemScreenSelectCallbacks.
evidence: Callers are the shop/item state machine functions Ui_Window_RegisterEventContextB, Ui_ShopWindow_Ctor and maybe_Ui_State_HandleEvent, but the record owner is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_State_Reset
summary: Releases the live reference at +0x2C (via the misnamed Ui_MessageWindow_SetStatusTextByType), zero-fills the 0x20-byte block at +4 and clears +0x24, returning the previous state id at +4.
evidence: No callers, and both callees are misnamed, so the release/memset sequence is clear but the record owner is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetMode
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_SetMode(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 layoutIndex, u32 arg3)
summary: Selects a message-window layout mode, rebuilds the panes through Ui_MessageWindow_RebuildPanes and hides both window sides (slots +0x18 at +0x138/+0x1DE4 and +0xE50).
evidence: Named callees Ui_MessageWindow_RebuildPanes and Ui_ListWindow_Create are visible, but the decompilation loses self and several registers (unaff_r4/r5/r7/r8), so the mode field cannot be verified.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_WantsInstantText
summary: Layout-mode query: returns 1 for any mode other than 2, and in mode 2 returns 0 only when the wide-layout entry's +0x46 byte is 1; otherwise 1.
evidence: Four named window builders call it, but the +0x46 test is only described, not proven to mean 'instant text' - the polarity could equally be 'needs rebuild'.

name: maybe_Ui_PushCommandSequence
summary: Pushes up to four 4-byte command words into the 16-byte FIFO at queue+4/+8: ids 0x104/0x105/0x106 for the three optional flag bytes and a final 0x103 (or 0x107 when the fourth flag is clear).
evidence: The recovered body (previously unreadable) shows a capacity-checked FIFO writer, not a UI sequence: the receiver is an anonymous ring buffer and ids 0x103..0x107 are not decoded anywhere, so the subsystem stays unproven.

name: maybe_Actor_DispatchComponentMessage
summary: Broadcasts one message to the actor's 32 component slots at self+0xE9C: slots whose vtable +0xE8 accepts it also get +0x134 and +0x120, and a second pass calls +0xF4 with +0x11C as fallback.
evidence: The 32-slot loop is the same one as the named Actor_NotifyComponentEvent (0x001CB624) and dispatches virtual slots, so 'dispatch a component message' is honest, while the old 'set flag' had no support.

name: maybe_Actor_ShouldSkipUpdate
summary: Actor predicate combining virtual +0x170, the +0xE8(0x7D) feature test, the byte at self+0xB148 against self+0xB108 and virtual +0x184 (fallback f_3A == 5).
evidence: The only caller is the equally doubtful Ui_PartyPanel_AllMembersUnavailable, which does not fit an actor predicate, and the 1/0 direction (update vs skip) is not provable from the body.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_ResetVirtual
summary: Broadcasts Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildrenUpdate and forwards the widget to its virtual slot +0x84 together with the global data pointer 0x007BE72E.
evidence: The named callee is confirmed, but the assembly passes a data pointer (g_paneNameCasino) rather than a mode value, so 'reset' versus 'apply name table' remains open.

name: maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_UpdateTransform
summary: Scene-node update override: after Field_SceneNode_NotifyChildrenUpdate it forwards the child handle at self+0x89 to virtual +0x84 when the handle exists.
evidence: Bracketed by the Ui_GuideWindow_Delete / maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_DtorDelete pair, but the virtual target and the caller (maybe_Field_SceneObject_InitFromRecordB) are unnamed, so only the node-update shape is certain.

name: maybe_Ui_StatusWindow_Dtor
summary: Destructor destroying the nine 0x36C-byte character slots at +0x13C, reinstalling the composite-window vtable, unlinking the window lists and freeing the block.
evidence: std_destroy_range with 9 x 0x36C slots plus g_uiCompositeWindowVtable is visible, but the status-window class name comes only from the prefix and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_SubTable_Dtor
summary: Non-deleting destructor of a small object owning a three-entry sub-table: installs g_uiCardTableVtable, clears state bytes, destroys the three 0x10-byte entries, frees the block and returns self.
evidence: The g_uiCardTableVtable store is the only class hint; the twin 0x001E4B4C is called by Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_Reset, so the owning class is still unconfirmed.

name: maybe_Ui_Array_DestroyThunk
signature: void maybe_Ui_Array_DestroyThunk(u32 array, void* elementDtor, u32 arg3, u32 count)
summary: 24-byte Thumb thunk that tail-calls std_destroy_range with base and element size taken from caller-saved r5/r6.
evidence: The body still reads unaff_r5/unaff_r6 and there are no callers; only the call target (std_destroy_range) is trustworthy.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_DestroySubObjects
summary: Unlinks the child node at (+0xD8)+0xC8 from its ring, clears both links and destroys the nine 0x14-byte records at (+0xD8)+0x10 via std_destroy_range; returns the sprite.
evidence: No bl targets this address (it is vtable-reached) and the element dtor 0x001C3858 is unnamed, so the class is inferred from the Field2D layout only.

name: maybe_Gfx_Movie_IsEndedOrPlayable
summary: Returns 1 when the controller latch (f_1F, audioFormat in the stale struct) is set or Gfx_Movie_IsPlayable(handle) succeeds, else 0 - i.e. 'stop advancing this movie'.
evidence: Only callee is the confident Gfx_Movie_IsPlayable, but with no caller the exact predicate meaning (ended, or playable) cannot be named better.

name: maybe_Ui_Anim_SetStateId
summary: Resets the animation object through 0x001DBC30 (currently misnamed Ui_Overlay_Shutdown) when its controller/frame/id state is set, then stores the new state id at anim+8.
evidence: Five callers, only two named (Gfx_Overlay_DrawSprite, Cutscene_ApplyLayoutMode), so the class is not pinned down and the reset callee is misnamed.

name: maybe_Gfx_MoviePlayer_Dtor
summary: Destructor installing the vtables g_moviePlayerDtorVtable / g_moviePlayerSubObjectVtable, releasing the read-request block at +0x454, destroying the embedded sub-objects at words 4 and 5 and freeing the player.
evidence: The vtable constants and sub-object teardown are visible, but two of the three callees (SaveData_ResetAllSaveData, Text_NgWord_CloseService) are obvious misnomers here, so the class is inferred from layout only.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelRow_DrawPane
summary: Builds a one-element pane list containing the row itself and passes it with the composite at self+0x38 to Ui_CompositeWindow_DrawPanes.
evidence: One named callee and a two-instruction body; no caller confirms the row class or that this is a vtable draw override.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_ResetSequence
summary: Resets a panel sequence: releases the card slots through Ui_PokerCards_ResetCardSlots, clears the running flag f_60 and installs the default step-handler pair from g_uiPartyPanelSlotObjectCallbacks.
evidence: Both named callees and the callback table are visible, but no caller names the object, so 'panel sequence' stays a structural label.

name: maybe_Ui_PanelState_SetDurationFromSlot
signature: void maybe_Ui_PanelState_SetDurationFromSlot(UiPanelSequence* panelSequence, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 slotArg)
summary: Chooses the sequence step pair: when the bound slot is absent or Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed(slot->f_1E18) is not 1 it sets a 5-frame wait and the long callback pair, otherwise it re-registers the card slots and uses the short pair.
evidence: Named callees Ui_PokerCards_ResetCardSlots and Ui_PromptRef_IsFirstChoiceConfirmed are visible, but the duration constants have no name and there is no caller.

name: maybe_Container_FixedArray_Remove
summary: Removes the head element of an inline array of 0x58-byte slots: releases the element at +8, moves the following block down over +4, zeroes the count at +0x5C and returns the removed element pointer.
evidence: The element release and 0x58-byte move are visible, but the two callees (Os_ThreadEntry, Ui_Message_SetNameArgs3) are misnamed and there is no caller to distinguish Remove from Clear.

name: maybe_Ui_Sequence_DeleteThunk
summary: 8-byte Thumb deleting-destructor thunk: calls Ui_Sequence_Dtor and then the free helper 0x0010F6CC; the real arguments arrive in r5/r6, so the decompiled parameter list is fabricated.
evidence: Body still depends on unaff_r5/unaff_r6; the clean ARM twin at 0x001F200C confirms only the dtor+free shape.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_GetOrCreateBalloon
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Ui_GetOrCreateBalloon(BattleBalloonUi* balloonUi, int slot, u8* outFlag)
summary: Returns the balloon object for a slot when it passes the virtual checks +0xD8/+0x10/+0x14 (and sets *outFlag when the slot differs from slot 0); otherwise clears the stale pointer and re-links the model through BattleUnit_GetLinkedModelByIndex.
evidence: The only callee is the named BattleUnit_GetLinkedModelByIndex, but there are no callers to prove the object is a battle balloon.

name: maybe_Menu_ClearPendingFlagA
summary: Menu callback-table slot: resets the list at self+0x4D78 with Menu_ResetListAndRelease and clears the byte at self+0x423D.
evidence: The 40-byte body is identical to 0x0020E554/0x0020E6CC/0x0020EE1C and each copy sits in a different menu callback-table entry, so the action is certain but the meaning of the cleared byte is not.

name: maybe_Menu_ClearPendingFlagB
summary: Menu callback-table slot: Menu_ResetListAndRelease(self+0x4D78) then clears the byte at self+0x423D; same body as 0x0020D430.
evidence: Registered in the second adjacent menu callback-table entry (0x00726DC0); identical to the A copy, so the letter suffix only distinguishes the table slot.

name: maybe_Menu_ClearPendingFlagC
summary: Menu callback-table slot: Menu_ResetListAndRelease(self+0x4D78) then clears the byte at self+0x423D; same body as 0x0020D430.
evidence: Third adjacent menu callback-table entry (0x00726E20); identical body, so the cleared flag's meaning remains unknown.

name: maybe_Menu_ClearPendingFlagD
summary: Menu callback-table slot: Menu_ResetListAndRelease(self+0x4D78) then clears the byte at self+0x423D; same body as 0x0020D430.
evidence: Fourth adjacent menu callback-table entry (0x00726E38); identical body, so the cleared flag's meaning remains unknown.

name: maybe_Menu_Camp_FinishGesture
summary: Once the actor animation frame passes f_2C it plays animation 4 when Field_NpcCheckSight(actor) is set, else animation 0 when 0x00669DD4(actor) is set.
evidence: Only Field_NpcCheckSight is confidently named; the animation setter 0x005E7848 and 0x00669DD4 are unnamed and the sole caller is the misnamed Battle_TextWindow_Release, so the camp context is unsupported.

name: maybe_Ui_Bar_StartFadeInOnRecords
signature: void maybe_Ui_Bar_StartFadeInOnRecords(void* records, int channel, unsigned int value)
summary: Starts a fade-in with the given value on three 0xC-stride records, using each record's +8 word for channel 0 and its +0xC word otherwise.
evidence: The only callee is the named Ui_Bar_StartFadeIn and the loop is a plain broadcast to three records; nothing in the body or neighbours mentions a camp or slot parameters, which is what the old name claimed.

name: maybe_Ui_ReleaseOverlay
summary: Releases the optional child object held at owner+0xC8 through its virtual slot +4 and clears the pointer.
evidence: Two instructions plus a null store; the +0xC8 slot is shared with the overlay task objects handled by 0x00215320, but the member type is unproven.

name: maybe_Ui_Overlay_BindEntrySlots
summary: Binds an overlay entry's two slot handles: when f_BC exists it calls 0x004C395C and, if f_C0 exists, re-binds f_BC with f_C0's +0x48 value through 0x004C397C.
evidence: All three callers are confidently named (Ui_Overlay_ApplySlotSetup, Ui_Overlay_ClearEntries, Ui_Overlay_AddEntry), so the receiver is an overlay entry; only the two helpers remain unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_InitChildWindow
summary: Initialises a part's child row/window at +0x124: formats it through Ui_ItemRow_Format, hides the null-button state via func_003B1F88(...,0), sets the animation reference at +0x174 to its frame and tail-calls the owner virtual +0x24.
evidence: Only caller Ui_SpritePart_CreateFromDesc allocates the 0x1C8-byte block and calls Ui_Part_Ctor, which fits, but the initialised child is not independently identified.

name: maybe_Ui_ResourceIcon_FinishLoad
summary: Tail of an icon load: creates the shared 0x98-byte object, stores it in the global 0x007BE310, resolves the icon record through the data manager, applies it to the render object and switches the icon to the finished state (+0x14 = 1, +0x18 = 8).
evidence: Body is heavily damaged (Ghidra dropped the argument registers, so the initialised object and the stored global are invisible) and there is no caller; only the two state writes and the data-manager lookup are certain.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_BeginLoadStep
summary: Drains the queued work with func_0062F070/func_0010EBD8, clears the status word f_814, starts a load through the named maybe_Save_BeginLoad(uiManager) and sets state byte f_810 = 1.
evidence: The recovered body (previously unreadable) calls maybe_Save_BeginLoad on the UI manager singleton and then sets state 1; nothing in it aborts, so the old 'Abort' verb was wrong.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_Finish
summary: Ends a load task: drains the queued work, resets the transform block at f_718 (func_006722D8), clears the status word f_824, notifies the UI manager's loader (func_002CDB5C) and sets state byte f_820 = 1.
evidence: Recovered body shares the drain + UI-manager loader steps with 0x003F3134 (Start) and differs by the 0x006722D8 transform reset, which supports a finish step but no caller names the task class.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_Start
signature: void maybe_Save_LoadTask_Start(SaveTask* task, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Starts a load task: clears task+4, fetches the UI manager, calls its loader (func_002CDB5C -> Save_LoadSlotHeader neighbour) and sets the task state byte at +0 to 1.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_Window_WaitForAnimC and the callees are the shared UI-manager loader, which fits a start step but does not prove the task class.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_SelectMode
summary: Load-task step: resets the transform block at f_718, clears f_824, then either sets bit 0x10000 and mode 1 (when uiManager+0xE3C0 == 3, calling the UI loader) or resets the UI list state and sets mode 2; stores the mode at f_820.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x003F3180 and shares the Save_LoadTask f_820/f_824 fields, so both belong to the save/load task step family; the 'StepB' label carried no information and the body is a mode choice, not an abort.

name: maybe_Save_LoadTask_SelectModeB
summary: Second copy of the load-task mode choice: sets bit 0x10000 + mode 1 and calls the UI manager loader when uiManager+0xE3C0 == 3, else resets the list state (maybe_Ui_ListState_Reset) and sets mode 2.
evidence: The doc itself notes that the callers are unnamed and not menus, so Ui_Menu_SetModeState was unsupported; the body is identical to 0x003F3160 and writes the same f_820 field of the save/load task.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SetChildColorFromRecord
signature: void maybe_Ui_Window_SetChildColorFromRecord(UiWindow* window, u32 arg2, const u32* record)
summary: Tail fragment that picks a colour word from a record (rec+4, or rec+0xC when the caller's Z flag is set) and forwards it to Ui_Window_SetChildColor together with the pane id from window+0x10.
evidence: The ldreq consumes the caller's condition flags (in_ZR), so this fragment is damaged and not self-contained; the only callee is the named Ui_Window_SetChildColor.

name: maybe_Ui_List_HandleInputAlt
summary: List-window step handler: bits 0x102 go to Ui_List_HandleInputPad, bit 0x10 returns early, otherwise it lazily creates the shared row widget, forwards the axis vector through listWidget vt+0x3C and plays animation 0x21 or 0x2E.
evidence: Recovered body confirms a list-window input step (Ui_List_HandleInputPad plus the anim controller), but the receiver class is still anonymous, so the '.Alt' suffix stays positional.

name: maybe_Ui_List_HandleInputB
summary: List-window input handler: on accept mask 0x142 it stores the row id and plays animation 6 or 7, bit 4 plays 4 and bit 8 plays 0x3B if the row allows it, bit 1 forwards the axis vector; finally refreshes the row-flag widget.
evidence: Recovered body is the same template as 0x0025C1DC/0x0025E380/0x0025E4EC with different animation ids, so the handler role is solid but the owning window class and the '.B' distinction are not.

name: maybe_Ui_PaneList_OnInput
signature: void maybe_Ui_PaneList_OnInput(UiPaneList* page, u32 inputMask, u32 p2, u32 p3, u32 p4)
summary: Row-list input handler: on accept mask it stores the row id and plays animation 0x2A/0x28, bit 4 plays 0x20, bit 8 plays 0x3B and bit 1 forwards the axis vector through the list vt+0x3C.
evidence: Named callees Ui_RowData_AtIndex and Ui_Window_SetRowParamsAndRefresh are visible, but the body uses unaff_r4/r5/r6 so the receiver is unproven and there is no direct caller (vtable-only).

name: maybe_Ui_PaneList_OnInput_Anim0B
summary: Row-list input handler variant: accept mask plays animation 0xB or 9, bit 4 plays 4, bit 8 plays 0x3B and bit 1 forwards the axis vector; refreshes the row-flag widget at the end.
evidence: Recovered body is the 0x0025C1DC template with animation ids 0xB/9; the missing function name for the owning window is why the '.Anim0B' tag stays.

name: maybe_Ui_PaneList_OnInput_Anim1B
summary: Row-list input handler variant: accept mask plays animation 0x1B or 0x19, bit 4 plays 4, bit 8 plays 0x3B and bit 1 forwards the axis vector; refreshes the row-flag widget at the end.
evidence: Recovered body is the 0x0025C1DC template with animation ids 0x1B/0x19; the owning window class is still unnamed.

name: maybe_Ui_Panel_HandleInput_2
summary: Panel input step: bits 0x102 go to Ui_TwoTabCursor_OnInput, bit 4 runs func_0021DF40, bit 0x10 runs func_0021E124 and otherwise the axis vector is forwarded; plays animation 0xF or 0xC depending on the branch.
evidence: Body is damaged (halt_baddata, coprocessor_ calls) and there is no caller; only the input-mask skeleton and the list-widget anim calls are reliable.

name: maybe_Ui_LoadScreen_PumpSaveTask
summary: Per-frame pump of a load screen: dispatches the save task (Save_Task_DispatchStep) when the timer is idle and otherwise steps the load window at self->loadWindow with the timer.
evidence: The body is badly damaged (halt_baddata, coprocessor_/software_interrupt pseudo-calls) so only the Save_Task_DispatchStep and loadWindow calls are real; no caller confirms the screen class.

name: Ui_Row_ApplyDefaultIconSet
summary: Builds the default seven-entry icon row on the stack with Ui_Row_SetDefaultIconSet and applies it to the unit through func_0037EA64(row, 0, unit), then discards the row.
evidence: The whole body is the named Ui_Row_SetDefaultIconSet followed by the unit application, and both callers (Model_SetSlotState, maybe_Battle_ActionSequence_DispatchActorEvent) are 3D battle-model code that needs the default icon set.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_AdvancePaneScript
summary: Steps the battle command pane to page 0x17 through the window vtable +0x4C and, when the flag word at self+0x234 is set, refreshes the party name lines and calls the sub-pane's +0x2C slot.
evidence: Body is damaged (Battle_Ui_RefreshPartyNameLines is called with no arguments and the second call is an unrecovered jump table) and there are no callers.

name: maybe_Ui_ListItemValue_Ctor
summary: Constructor of a small UI record that embeds a text line: stores the vtable word, the caller's value at +4, initialises the embedded text line with Ui_TextLine_Reset(self+3) and copies a literal pair into +0xC/+0xD.
evidence: The recovered body (previously unreadable) is clearly a constructor with an embedded text line, but nothing names the owner class or what the value at +4 means, so 'ListItemValue' stays a guess.

name: maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_EndTransition
summary: Releases the window's children with Ui_Root_ReleaseAll(window+4, 0) and then queries (vt+0x14) and commits (vt+0x10) a pending command on the pane-animation object at window+0xC.
evidence: Only callee is the named Ui_Root_ReleaseAll and both vtable calls are indirect, so neither the shop context nor the 'end transition' verb is proven.

name: maybe_Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventA
signature: void maybe_Ui_SlideWindow_OnEventA(UiSlideWindow* slideWindow, int eventId, int arg3, int b)
summary: Event handler mapping ids 2/3 onto controller states 1/0 through the +0x14 slot of the widget at self+0x4C, running Field_PathMover_SnapToNearestPathPoint for id 4 and finally forwarding the raw id to the slide callback's +0x84 slot.
evidence: Body is damaged (unaff_r4..r6, in_lr, unrecovered jump table); the only named callee is the path snap, so the receiver class and the id-4 branch are not proven.

name: maybe_Ui_PaneGroup_DeletingDtor
summary: Scalar deleting destructor of a pane-group-like object: installs the class vtable, runs the named Ui_LayoutRefList_Dtor on the embedded layout reference list and frees the object through the virtual deleter 0x0010F6CC.
evidence: The trailing virtual deleter proves a deleting destructor and the callee Ui_LayoutRefList_Dtor is confident, but no vtable row or caller identifies the concrete class.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DtorDeleteF
summary: Deleting destructor of an unnamed Ui_Drawable-derived class: reinstalls the vtable, runs Ui_Drawable_Dtor and frees the object.
evidence: Confident callee Ui_Drawable_Dtor plus the standard dtor+delete idiom; identical copies at 0x003B498C/0x003B567C and no vtable row or caller names the class.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeleteB
summary: Deleting destructor of another Ui_Drawable-derived class: reinstalls the vtable, runs Ui_Drawable_Dtor and frees the object; same body as 0x00299470.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x00299470/0x003B567C; the callee is confident but no vtable row or caller identifies this class, so the letter suffix only distinguishes the copy.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeleteC
summary: Third identical deleting destructor for a sibling Ui_Drawable-derived class: reinstalls the vtable, runs Ui_Drawable_Dtor and frees.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x003B498C/0x00299470; class unnamed, so the guess keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_SetFlag4
signature: void maybe_Ui_Pane_SetFlag4(UiPane* pane, u32 p1, int set)
summary: Sets or clears bit 2 of the pane state byte at +0x204, tells the child widget whether the byte became zero (slot +0x18) and recomputes the transform via func_001A62E4.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_AttachListNodes
summary: Splices the two optional intrusive list nodes described by 0x0072AF1C into the owner's lists at +0x588 and +0x568 and sets the widget's back-pointers; no function pointer is ever called.
evidence: Only callee Snd_DetachChannel is misnamed here (it is a list insert), and the static descriptor 0x0072AF1C's contents are unknown, so the list role is certain but the node meaning is not.

name: maybe_Ui_Pane_SetEnabledByLookup
summary: Resolves a list-item reference: a resolved row sets bit 1 of the pane flag word, an unresolved one clears it, and the child widget is told whether the pane is now empty.
evidence: Callee Ui_ListItemRef_ResolveRow confirms param 2 is a list-item ref, but the meaning of bit 1 is still inferred from the set/clear pattern.

name: maybe_Anim_Clip_BuildLoopFragment
signature: unsigned int maybe_Anim_Clip_BuildLoopFragment(AnimClipSet* clipSet, unsigned int trackStep)
summary: Loop body of Anim_Clip_Build: walks the 0x1C-byte track descriptors, counts the steps that are present and calls Anim_Clip_ConvertTracks for the next output pointers.
evidence: Ghidra split the function with everything in unaff_ registers, so only the named callee Anim_Clip_ConvertTracks fixes the family, not the role; the caller Ui_Sprite_ApplyParams does not help.

name: maybe_Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgsTail
summary: Not a real entry point: the second bl plus epilogue inside Ui_SakusenWindow_BuildMessageArgs (0x002A29A8); the symbol exists only so the merge does not invent a function.
evidence: Body is halt_baddata, the sole caller is the parent function and the assembly shows a mid-function bl/add sp/pop {pc} sequence.

name: maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion
signature: void maybe_Field_Actor_SetNutMotion(void* actor, int useNut, int seekLastFrame)
summary: Selects the actor's 'Nut' motion when useNut is non-zero (state word +0x288 = 0) and the default 'Open' motion otherwise (+0x288 = -1), plays it through the animation owner at +0xB8 and, when seekLastFrame is set, jumps to the clip's last frame.
evidence: The inline 'Nut' literal and the default name pointer that resolves to 'Open' are visible, but there is no caller to confirm the actor class or the flag polarity.

name: maybe_Field_Object2D_AdvanceTouchTransition
summary: Steps the object's touch state machine (Field_Object2D_RunTouchTransition) and returns 1 while the state byte has not reached the terminal value 3, i.e. 'still running'.
evidence: The disassembly (bl then ldrb/cmp #3/eor #1) confirms the 'not finished' return, but no named caller identifies the object class.

name: maybe_Field_SceneObject_RefreshTouchEvent
summary: Rebuilds the object's cached interaction record: calls Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent(type 5, actor id or 0xFF, object position, 0xFFFFFFFF) and copies its id, three flag bytes and four coordinates into +0x4D8..+0x4F4; returns 1.
evidence: Named callee Field_Object2D_CreateTouchEvent and the field copy show this refreshes a cached touch event rather than answering a query, which is what the old 'QueryState' name suggested.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SelectStateByFlag
summary: Asks Item_HasSpecialRangeItem whether a special flag range is set, requests controller state 3 or 0 accordingly and commits the request through the sub-component vtable +0x10 when it succeeds.
evidence: The only callee is the named Item_HasSpecialRangeItem and the body only drives subComponent35C slots f_14/f_10; no caller or vtable row identifies the window class.

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdatePayout
signature: void maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdatePayout(void* jackpotScreen, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int b)
summary: Per-frame jackpot step: waits on the cue and roulette window animations and then switches the step function to the next entry of g_uiJackpotScreenCallbacks (state 6 when a reel stops).
evidence: Callees include maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateIntro and the jackpot callback table, but the state ids 4/5/6/7 and the 'payout' verb remain unexplained.

name: maybe_Ui_ListState_Reset
summary: Resets the UI manager's list/scroll state: clears counters and flag bytes, zero-fills the tail, allocates the 0x1820-byte table through 0x0051BB08, restores the 0x5E cursor, 0xFF sentinel and page count 6 and locks the state mutex.
evidence: Only caller is the equally inferred maybe_Save_LoadTask_SelectModeB, which passes the UI manager singleton; the constants and mutex fit a list-state reset but no named callee confirms it.

name: maybe_Ui_Sequence_AdvanceTimedStep
signature: unsigned int maybe_Ui_Sequence_AdvanceTimedStep(void* step, int* context)
summary: Timed sequence step: increments the frame counter, plays a sound effect at frame 0 and again at frame 0x49, and reports done when the sub-object is absent or its +0x24 float equals the completion constant.
evidence: The only named callee is Sound_PlaySeCached and there is no caller, so the owning sequence and the two SE cues stay unidentified.

name: maybe_Anim_Owner_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of an object owning an animation instance: stores the vtable, destroys the embedded Anim_Instance at +0xFC, runs the 0x002650C4 module teardown and frees the object.
evidence: Callee Anim_Instance_Dtor is confident and the trailing free is the deleting-dtor idiom, but no vtable row or caller names the concrete class.

name: maybe_Ui_CreateSpriteByName
summary: Lazily creates the shared UI object for the UI heap (vtable g_uiMessageWindowBaseVtable2, the same block shape as 0x001C4FF4) and applies the caller's name string to its sub-object at +0x48.
evidence: The only caller is the uncertain maybe_Field_Object2D_SyncAttachedNodes and the callee that applies the string is misnamed Party_Status_SetMemberValueByRatio, so 'sprite' has no support; the lazy-singleton + set-name shape is certain.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_UpdateSelection
summary: List-window selection step: on accept mask 0x142 it takes the new row id, on bit 4 it forces a retry id, on bit 1 it forwards the axis vector; then stores the id, refreshes the row widget with Ui_ListWidget_SetRowFromRecord and triggers the page animation.
evidence: The recovered body is the same template as 0x004A1704 and drives Ui_ListWidget_SetRowFromRecord plus a sub-pane vtable, i.e. a UI list window step; 'Actor_ActionSeq_RunChoice2' described an actor action sequence that the body does not contain.

name: maybe_Ui_ListWindow_UpdateSelectionB
summary: Second copy of the list-window selection step: releases sub-widgets, forwards the stored axis vector through the list widget's vt+0x3C, compares the returned row id with the stored selection and refreshes the row via Ui_ListWidget_SetRowFromRecord.
evidence: Body is the same template as 0x002E9CD0 at the f_D80/f_3AC/f_D94 offsets and the shared callee Ui_ListWidget_SetRowFromRecord is used by many list windows, so 'CommandPanel' was too specific.

name: maybe_Field_Object_UpdateHook
summary: Unrecoverable 28-byte hook: only flag-register arithmetic, one call to 0x003AAFCA and two halt_baddata sites were recovered.
evidence: Body built from in_ZR/in_NG/in_OV/in_CY (damaged decompilation) with no named callees; only the positional evidence from its four overlay neighbours remains.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_ResetAndSelectFirst
summary: Forwards the reset command to the node's children (0x005E7594, the twin of Field_SceneNode_ForwardCommandToChildren) and then selects entry 0 of the keyed list at self+0x60.
evidence: Both callees are named (Container_KeyedList_SelectEntry and the forward-command helper) and the body is identical to 0x003E60F0, so the action is a reset/first-entry selection - 'Destruct' was unsupported.

name: maybe_Field_SceneNode_ResetAndSelectFirstB
summary: Same body as 0x002FB644: forwards the reset command to the children and reselects keyed-list entry 0; the node class (actor vs prop) is not determined.
evidence: Identical body to 0x002FB644 with the same named callees, and neither address has a caller, so the 'actor / stop action object' reading had no support.
